hypothesis: Retaining exact HTTP body bytes while varying input chunk boundaries should preserve the parsed-value oracle. This targets a representation interaction without changing the original data or expected result.
scope: One Python HTTPX adapter; no task/repository/candidate IDs in the implementation. Unsupported trials remain in the17-trial denominator.
inputs: Original corpus, frontend, public issue, source test metadata. The older cohort supplies only the17-trial list and source paths.
semantics: HTTP content is a byte sequence. Require an existing streamed test of the same issue-named semantic iterator. Exclude raw/chunk/line/text observers and any buffered-test receiver access beyond its single semantic iteration.
preservation: One original content expression becomes a generator of adjacent slices of exactly the same bytes. Closed literal/parametrized bytes domains only; retain all complete-test assertions and other inputs.
ordering: chunk-size rank then source retrieval rank, path and test position
execution: All source controls must pass. Require exact test transport and two independent controlled failures of the first failing program. No later replacement within a trial.

authorities.role: Public HTTPX response interface; also corroborated by frozen repository source controls

limitations: This limited adapter does not establish applicability to all iterable or callback APIs.
A representation relation cannot by itself prove every source oracle valid. Audit every emitted full test.
This is development evidence; independent tasks are still needed.
